+ "Converts a float tensor to a quantized tensor by applying a scale/zero-point transform:\n\nresult = round(input / scale) + zero_point\n\nThe exact operation sequence (where ftype is the input type):\n\nr_div: ftype = real_div(input, scale) r_rnd: ftype = round(r_div) Z: ftype = cast(zero_point) r_zero: ftype = add(r_rnd, Z) r_clip: ftype = clip(r_zero, min_value<dtype>, max_value<dtype>) result: dtype = cast(r_clip)\n\nSupported quantized types: `ui1/bool`, `ui2`, `si2`, `ui4`, `si4`, `ui8`, `si8`\n\n**Per-axis quantization:** If `axis` is provided, `scale` and `zero_point` must be 0-D or 1-D tensors that will be broadcast along the specified axis.\n\nNote: Unlike DequantizeOp, QuantizeOp does NOT support N-D blockwise quantization.\n\n**Per-tensor quantization:** If `axis` is not defined and `scale` is a scalar, the operation is per-tensor.\n\n**Specialized formats:** - MX scaling: `f4e2m1`, `f6e3m2`, `f6e2m3`, `f8e4m3`, `f8e5m2` with `f8e8m0` scale and blocksize 32 - NVFP4: `f4e2m1` with `f8e4m3` scale and blocksize 16"
+ "Converts a quantized tensor to a float tensor by applying a scale/zero-point transform:\n\nresult = scale * (input - zero_point) + min\n\nThe exact operation sequence (where dtype is the output type):\n\nq_cast: dtype = cast(input) Z: dtype = cast(zero_point) q_center: dtype = sub(q_cast, Z) result_bias: dtype = mul(q_center, scale) result: dtype = add(result_bias, min)\n\nSupported quantized types: `ui1/bool`, `ui2`, `si2`, `ui4`, `si4`, `ui8`, `si8`, `f16`, `f32`, `bf16`\n\n**Per-axis dequantization:** If `axis` is provided, `scale`, `zero_point`, and `min` must be 0-D or 1-D tensors that will be broadcast along the specified axis.\n\n**Blockwise dequantization:** If `axis` is not defined and `scale` is a tensor, the operation uses blockwise semantics.\n\nIn blockwise mode:\n- `input`, `scale`, and `result` have the same rank\n- `zero_point` and `min` must be broadcast-compatible to `scale`\n- `block_size[i] = input.shape[i] / scale.shape[i]` must be an integer for each dimension\n\nAlgorithm (illustrated for rank-3):\n\nresult[i, j, k] = scale[i0, j0, k0] * (input[i, j, k] - zero_point[i0, j0, k0]) + min[i0, j0, k0]\n\nwhere:\ni0 = floor(i / block_size[0])\nj0 = floor(j / block_size[1])\nk0 = floor(k / block_size[2])\nblock_size[m] = input.shape[m] / scale.shape[m]\n\n**Per-tensor dequantization:** If `axis` is not defined and `scale` is a scalar, the operation is per-tensor.\n\n**Specialized formats:** - MX scaling: `f4e2m1`, `f6e3m2`, `f6e2m3`, `f8e4m3`, `f8e5m2` with `f8e8m0` scale and blocksize 32 - NVFP4: `f4e2m1` with `f8e4m3` scale and blocksize 16"

- "Convert a float to a si8 or ui8 tensor by applying a scale / bias transform:\nresult = (input / scale) + zero_point\n\nLet ftype the type of input. The exact operation can be described as:\nr_div: ftype = real_div(input, scale)\nr_rnd: ftype = round(r_div)\nZ: ftype = cast(zero_point)\nr_zero: ftype = add(r_rnd, Z)\nr_clip: ftype = clip(r_zero, min_value<dtype>, max_value<dtype>)\nresult: dtype = cast(r_clip)\n\nIf `scale`/`zero_point` is a vector, the operation is broadcasted on `axis`. If `axis` is not defined, `scale`/`zero_point` must be a scalar."
- "Convert a si8/ui8 tensor to a float tensor by applying a scale / bias transform:\nresult =  scale * (input - zero_point) + min\n\nLet itype the type of input. The exact operation can be described as:\nq_cast: dtype = cast(q)\nZ: dtype = cast(zero_point)\nq_center: dtype = sub(q_cast, zero_point)\nresult_bias: dtype = mul(q_center, scale)\nresult: dtype = add(result_bias, min)\n\nIf `scale`/`zero_point` is a vector, the operation is broadcasted on `axis`. If `axis` is not defined, `scale`/`zero_point` must be a scalar."
